claims.text: Rapid exploration of the vast HEA compositional space requires advanced design strategies and efficient computational tools.
CALPHAD calculations require both computational software and a thermodynamic database.
A hybrid CALPHAD-ML methodology is required to predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity in multicomponent RHEAs.
The computational cost of standard CALPHAD scales exponentially when the number of components exceeds five.
High-temperature thermodynamic databases for complex refractory systems are lacking, causing sparse or unreliable predictions.
An ML surrogate trained on sparse CALPHAD or DFT data can approximate the Gibbs free energies of liquid and solid phases over the full compositional space.
The ML surrogate can bypass exhaustive composition-grid searches.
Melting temperature can be obtained from the temperature at which the modeled liquid and solid Gibbs free energies are equal.
Entropy of fusion can be calculated from the temperature slope of the modeled Gibbs free energy.
Heat capacity can be calculated from the second temperature derivative of the modeled Gibbs free energy.
Configurational entropy and lattice distortion in BCC solid solutions and disordered liquids dominate RHEA thermodynamic stability and melting behavior.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the RHEA solid solution and raises its melting point relative to the constituent elements.
Interactions among refractory elements produce non-ideal solution behavior.
Standard linear mixing rules fail to capture the non-ideal thermodynamics of refractory HEAs.
CALPHAD becomes computationally prohibitive in high-dimensional alloy spaces because of a combinatorial explosion in phase-equilibrium calculations.
The proposed method may fail for alloys with unmodeled complex intermetallic precipitation or with phase behavior dominated by kinetic effects.
The hybrid method will predict melting temperature within ±50 K and entropy of fusion within ±10% of experimental values.
The hybrid method will reduce computational time by more than 99% relative to full CALPHAD grid searches.
A full 1 at.% CALPHAD grid search requires thousands of hours on a desktop for quinary systems and is infeasible for higher-order systems.
The method is valid for single-phase BCC solid solutions and liquids whose primary stability is governed by configurational entropy.
